title: Hims & Hers Expands Digital-First Access to Personalized Healthcare
content:
Hims & Hers Health, Inc. HIMS is fundamentally built around expanding access to healthcare by shifting traditionally fragmented, in-person experiences into a more seamless digital model. Its platform connects consumers to licensed providers, enabling telehealth consultations, digital prescriptions and online fulfillment, all designed to make care faster, and more convenient and affordable. By integrating these capabilities, HIMS aims to reduce longstanding barriers such as stigma, cost and limited provider availability, while delivering personalized care across a wide range of conditions.

Recent developments reinforce this access-driven strategy. Hims & Hers has continued to broaden the availability of treatments by partnering with Novo Nordisk to offer FDA-approved GLP-1 medications at more affordable prices and through multiple delivery formats, simplifying access for eligible patients. At the same time, it has expanded proactive care through new offerings such as multi-cancer early detection testing and its Labs platform, both of which are designed to make advanced diagnostics more accessible and actionable for everyday consumers.

Geographic expansion has further extended this mission. Through acquisitions and market entries, Hims & Hers is scaling its digital-first model globally, including in Canada and Europe, with a focus on bringing affordable, personalized care to populations where access has historically been limited. Together, these initiatives reflect a consistent effort to democratize healthcare — making high-quality, personalized care more accessible across conditions, formats and geographies.

Hims & Hers is scheduled to report first-quarter 2026 results on May 11, after the closing bell.

GDRX and TDOC Expanding Digital Healthcare Access

GoodRx Holdings, Inc. GDRX is advancing digital-first healthcare access by simplifying how consumers find, afford and receive treatments. GDRX has expanded condition-specific subscriptions, including services for hair loss and erectile dysfunction that combine virtual consultations, prescriptions and home delivery into a single streamlined experience, reducing barriers such as cost and inconvenience. At the same time, GoodRx continues to scale affordability through partnerships and pricing innovations. GoodRx enables access to high-cost therapies like GLP-1 treatments with transparent self-pay pricing, while also integrating savings directly at the pharmacy counter through programs like RxSmartSaver.

Teladoc Health, Inc. TDOC is advancing digital-first healthcare access by delivering comprehensive virtual care across physical and mental health needs through its Integrated Care and BetterHelp platforms. Teladoc Health connects patients, providers and systems to enable 24/7 access to services spanning preventive, primary, chronic and mental healthcare, improving outcomes while lowering costs. Teladoc Health recently enhanced its 24/7 Care service to treat a broader range of conditions, integrate specialist input and streamline referrals, further expanding access and care continuity through its technology-driven ecosystem.

title: Teladoc Q1 Preview: Profits seen improving, BetterHelp operations in focus
content:
[mature woman doctor stand and talk on mobile phone at home]
Miljan Živković/iStock via Getty Images

Teladoc Health’s (TDOC [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TDOC]) Q1 loss is projected to see a 26% improvement in its earnings on April 27, after market close, with continued improvement expected from its BetterHelp segment.

The consensus EPS Estimate is -$0.39, [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TDOC/earnings/estimates] while revenue is seen falling 3% to $610.59M. Ahead of the earnings, sentiment appears cautious as analysts have made no upward revisions [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TDOC/earnings/revisions] for earnings or revenue. Meanwhile, they have issued 2 and 19 downward revisions, respectively.

BetterHelp's revenue declined 9% in 2025, in line with its last four years’ performance, showing flat or declining revenue, high cost of user acquisition, high rates of seasonal churn, and lack of recurring revenue. 

However, the business has shown improvement following its acquisition of UpLift in April 2025.

“To date, early results validate a change in the model. In 2025, BetterHelp generated about $13 million in insurance revenue, with management expecting this to grow to $75–$90 million in 2026, representing a 6-7x increase from the previous year,” Seeking Alpha analyst Tyler Wiedwald [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4890017-teladoc-health-improving-fundamentals-support-a-turnaround-story] noted.

The management sees BetterHelp 2026 revenue falling between 7% and 0.5% (vs. 2025), with insurance revenue expected at $75 million to $90 million and an exit annualized revenue run rate above $100 million. Direct-to-consumer revenue is projected to be down 14% to 9%, while international revenue is expected to see double-digit growth.

Some optimism is also centered around PulseAI under Teledoc’s integrated care segment, which has often had the highest number of virtual visits within the overall industry.

“With the release of Pulse, Teladoc now has the opportunity to provide an AI-based classification system that identifies patients with chronic conditions that may be showing signs of deterioration and thereby creates opportunities for costly acute-care episodes. This separates them from the traditional model and improves their value proposition,” the analyst noted.

For the full year, Integrated Care revenue is expected to grow 0.4% to 3.9%, with a full-year adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.1% to 16.1%. U.S. integrated care members are forecast to range from 97 million to 100 million by year's end.

Teladoc expects full-year 2026 consolidated revenue between $2.47 billion and $2.59 billion. Adjusted EBITDA is forecast in the range of $266 million to $308 million, reflecting 2% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.

title: Are These Beaten-Down Stocks Generational Opportunities or Value Traps?
content:
Key Points

Teladoc's headwinds seem almost insurmountable right now. PayPal has strengths and opportunities that could allow it to bounce back.10 stocks we like better than PayPal ›

Some stocks saw massive surges during the early pandemic years because their businesses were well-positioned to perform well in that environment. Many of them have given back those gains, and then some, since then. Two corporations that fit this description are Teladoc Health(NYSE: TDOC) and PayPal(NASDAQ: PYPL). Both companies are down by more than 80% over the past five years. If they can recover, Teladoc and PayPal may offer patient investors who purchase their shares at current levels outstanding returns over the long run, making them potential generational buying opportunities. However, their shares could continue sinking if they fail to address their challenges. Should investors take a chance on Teladoc, PayPal, or both?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue »

1. Teladoc Health

Teladoc is a telemedicine specialist. Patients can get basic consultations with doctors from the comfort of their homes through its platform, along with prescriptions and referrals. In some cases, that gets the job done without patients needing to see doctors in person, which saves everyone involved time and money. Teladoc has established itself as a notable player. The company's ecosystem featured more than 100 million members as of the end of 2025.

Why, then, has Teladoc significantly lagged the market in recent years? Here are two reasons. First, the company encountered significant competition. Between other telehealth companies seeking to eat Teladoc's lunch, major corporations with deep existing ecosystems developing their own dedicated virtual conference platforms for telemedicine visits, and a shift back to in-person care, the company's total visits haven't grown much in recent years.

Teladoc Health has faced particular challenges in the virtual therapy niche where it competes through BetterHelp. Once its most important growth drivers, BetterHelp's memberships and revenue have been declining.

Second, Teladoc Health has remained unprofitable, partly due to high customer acquisition costs and the impact of acquisitions on its bottom line. Can Teladoc turn things around? The company has been expanding internationally while seeking third-party coverage for BetterHelp, which could help increase the service's appeal. However, Teladoc has had little success with that goal. Meanwhile, even though international revenue is growing at a good clip, investors should consider the possibility that Teladoc will, eventually, face the same challenges abroad.  In my view, the stock is unlikely to recover anytime soon. It's best to stay away.

2. PayPal

The popularity of e-commerce -- which requires digital payment methods -- soared during the pandemic. That allowed PayPal to post some of its best quarters ever. However, once things cooled down, the company's active accounts growth stalled, as did revenue and earnings growth. That said, I remain bullish on PayPal's future. Here are three reasons why. First, the company has developed a brand name and remains a trusted player in its niche of the fintech industry. That could be particularly important as the market continues to grow.

Second, PayPal has arguably built a strong competitive edge thanks to network effects. The company ended 2025 with 439 million active accounts (up 1.1% year over year in the fourth quarter), along with a massive total payment volume of $1.79 trillion for the year, up 7% from 2024.

PayPal's large payment volume and significant adoption among both businesses and consumers attract more players on both sides of the commerce equation. Third, PayPal has attractive growth opportunities ahead. One of the most exciting is its push into digital advertising. PayPal has a massive amount of data on consumer shopping habits and preferences at its disposal to help companies craft highly targeted ads. This high-margin opportunity could help boost the company's revenue and earnings in the long run, even if it takes a little while for PayPal to scale this business. So, PayPal remains a top stock to buy and hold, especially at current levels.

title: Earnings week ahead: MSFT, AAPL, GOOG, AMZN, META, XOM, CVX, KO, V, SBUX, F, GM, and more
content:
[Magnifying Glass On Top Of Bar Chart Showing Decling Performance]
DNY59/iStock via Getty Images

As earnings season hits its peak, the week ahead stands out as one of the most consequential reporting stretches of the year.

Five members of the Magnificent Seven, Apple (AAPL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL]), Microsoft (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), Amazon (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), Alphabet (GOOGL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOGL]), and Meta (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), headline the calendar, placing a sharp spotlight on AI monetization, cloud demand, digital advertising, and consumer ecosystems.

Beyond big tech, the week spans a remarkably broad cross-section of the global economy.

Energy majors Exxon Mobil (XOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM]), Chevron (CVX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CVX]), and ConocoPhillips (COP [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/COP]) will reflect commodity dynamics, while industrial bellwethers Caterpillar (CAT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CAT]), General Dynamics (GD [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GD]), and UPS offer a read on infrastructure, defense, and global logistics demand.

Consumer and payments giants like Coca-Cola (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO]), Starbucks (SBUX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SBUX]), Chipotle (CMG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CMG]), Visa (V [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/V]), and Mastercard (MA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MA]) will provide cues on spending resilience, and healthcare leaders Eli Lilly (LLY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/LLY]), Merck (MRK [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MRK]), AbbVie (ABBV [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ABBV]), and Amgen (AMGN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMGN]) will highlight innovation pipelines and demand durability.

The calendar further extends into autos, telecom, fintech, and emerging tech, with Ford (F [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/F]), GM, T-Mobile (TMUS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TMUS]), Verizon (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ]), Robinhood (HOOD [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/HOOD]), Roku (ROKU [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ROKU]), and Enphase Energy (ENPH [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ENPH]) adding depth across connectivity, retail investing, and clean energy.

Rounding out the week are names spanning digital platforms, materials, and semiconductors, including QUALCOMM (QCOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/QCOM]), Spotify (SPOT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/SPOT]), Booking Holdings (BKNG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BKNG]), First Solar (FSLR [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/FSLR]), and Vale (VALE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VALE]).

With leadership stocks and cyclical sectors reporting side by side, this week's earnings will deliver one of the most comprehensive snapshots yet of global growth, corporate spending, and market direction, and a critical test of whether elevated expectations around AI, consumption, and macro resilience can hold.

Below is a rundown of major quarterly updates anticipated in the week of April 20 to April 24:

MONDAY, APRIL 27

VERIZON COMMUNICATIONS (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ])

Verizon Communications (VZ [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ]) is set to report Q1 results before Monday’s open, with analysts expecting modest Y/Y growth in both revenue and earnings.

Wall Street maintains a Buy rating, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system remains more cautious at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/VZ/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing limited growth visibility.

SA VIEWS REMAIN MIXED:

Kenio Fontes recently downgraded the stock to Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891357-verizon-why-shareholders-should-fear-the-amazon-flywheel-downgrade], pointing to modest near-term momentum (2–3% revenue growth and 4–5% EPS guidance for 2026) amid intense competition from T-Mobile US and AT&T.

On the bullish side, The Alpha Analyst reiterates a Strong Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891143-verizon-stock-strong-buy-resilient-cash-flow-stable-valuation], viewing VZ as an income-focused play supported by resilient cash flows, ~9x forward earnings valuation, and robust capital return plans. Management’s focus on ~$5B in cost savings, disciplined capex, and steady free cash flow growth underpins dividend sustainability and buybacks.

In contrast, SA Investing Group Leader Stone Fox Capital maintains a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891802-verizon-path-back-down-to-40], citing structural growth challenges, high leverage, and limited exposure to next-generation growth areas. Despite its ~6% yield, concerns around flat wireless growth and reliance on legacy assets could pressure long-term valuation.

 	* Consensus Revenue Estimates: $34.86B

TUESDAY, APRIL 28

COCA-COLA (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO])

The Coca-Cola Company (KO [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO]) is set to report Q1 results before Tuesday’s open, with analysts expecting over 9% Y/Y growth in both revenue and earnings.

The company recently announced a $1B investment [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4571064-coca-cola-unveils-1b-south-africa-investment-plan-through-2030] in South Africa through 2030, alongside local bottling partners, aimed at expanding production, strengthening distribution, and driving product innovation, highlighting its asset-light, franchise-driven model.

Wall Street maintains a Buy rating, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system is more cautious at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/KO/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing valuation concerns.

SA author YR Research reiterates a Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4890277-coca-cola-the-retirement-dream], emphasizing Coca-Cola’s defensive appeal, consistent mid-single-digit organic growth, and strong dividend profile, with expected annual returns of 8–10%.

WEDNESDAY, APRIL 29

MICROSOFT CORPORATION (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), AMAZON.COM (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), META PLATFORMS (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), AND ALPHABET (GOOG [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOG])

Wednesday shapes up as a pivotal moment for Big Tech, with four “Magnificent 7” names. Microsoft (MSFT [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MSFT]), Meta Platforms (META [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/META]), Amazon (AMZN [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AMZN]), and Alphabet (GOOGL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GOOGL]) are all set to report after the market closes, placing the spotlight firmly on AI, cloud, and digital advertising trends.

Heading into earnings, the narrative remains centered [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4576930-the-earnings-tightrope-will-mag-7-bulls-pivot-to-bottom-fishing] on AI-driven growth versus margin pressure. Microsoft’s Azure momentum is key, though rising CapEx continues to divide opinion. Meta is viewed constructively on pullbacks despite mixed reception to recent AI developments, while Alphabet’s steady growth is tempered by heavy investments in AI and adjacent ventures. Amazon, meanwhile, is doubling down on AI and infrastructure through its massive AWS investments, with markets closely watching returns on capital.

Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy across all four names, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system takes a more measured stance with Hold ratings, reflecting valuation concerns.

However, SA author Gary Alexander rates Amazon a Sell [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4893417-amazon-sell-on-anthropic-deal-spike-valuation-doesnt-add-up], arguing its ~$2.7T valuation is difficult to justify despite recent momentum driven by AWS and AI partnerships.

Recent developments have kept the spotlight on the iPhone maker. A major leadership transition is underway, with Tim Cook set to move into an Executive Chairman role and John Ternus stepping in as CEO, signaling a stronger product and engineering focus.

Meanwhile, iPhone shipments in China rose 20% in Q1, supported by the latest iPhone cycle, pricing actions, and government incentives.

Wall Street remains bullish, with Morgan Stanley viewing the upcoming print as a potential “clearing event,” driven by solid momentum across iPhone, Mac, and Services.

However, Seeking Alpha’s Quant Rating stays at Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAPL/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], citing valuation concerns.

Chevron Corporation (CVX [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/CVX]) and Exxon Mobil Corporation (XOM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM]) are all set to report Q1 results before Friday’s open, with analysts expecting a mixed performance amid a volatile energy backdrop.

Recent developments highlight diverging narratives. Exxon has advanced its LNG ambitions, with its Golden Pass project [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4578804-exxon-qatarenergy-ship-first-lng-cargo-from-golden-pass-export-terminal] shipping its first cargo, while also exploring downstream portfolio optimization, including a potential sale of its Hong Kong retail network. However, Wolfe Research recently downgraded the stock, citing valuation concerns after its strong run.

Chevron, meanwhile, has resumed [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4578829-chevron-resumes-full-production-at-wheatstone-lng-after-cyclone-damage-shutdown] full production at its Wheatstone LNG facility following outage-related disruptions, though operational challenges, including a refinery incident in Texas, could weigh on near-term downstream performance.

Sentiment remains broadly constructive. Wall Street maintains Buy ratings on both names, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant system assigns Strong Buy ratings [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/XOM/ratings/quant-ratings#source=firstLevelUrl%3Asymbol%7CbiSectionAsset%3ARatingSummary%7CbiName%3AQuant_rating], supported by elevated oil prices and geopolitical tailwinds.

SA author views reflect this divergence. Asian Value Investor maintains a Strong Buy [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4889690-chevron-stock-growth-drivers-are-in-sync-with-valuation-and-technicals] on Chevron, citing its upstream leverage, strong balance sheet, and resilience to higher oil prices. In contrast, Exxon is rated Hold [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4889477-exxon-mobil-stock-price-drop-priced-in-everything-but-didnt-deeply-discount-it], with solid fundamentals largely priced in and technical indicators signaling caution despite continued operational strength.

title: 1 Internet Stock on Our Watchlist and 2 Facing Headwinds
content:
Consumer internet businesses are redefining how people engage with the world by giving them instant connectivity and convenience. This influence cuts both ways though because they have high exposure to the ups and downs of consumer spending, and the market seems to believe the tide is turning in the wrong direction - over the past six months, the industry has tumbled by 17.9%. This drop is a noticeable divergence from the S&P 500’s 4.8% return.

The elite companies can churn out earnings growth under any circumstance, however, and our mission at StockStory is to help you find them. Taking that into account, here is one resilient internet stock at the top of our wish list and two that may face trouble.

Two Consumer Internet Stocks to Sell:

Revolve (RVLV)

Market Cap: $1.96 billion

Launched in 2003 by software engineers Michael Mente and Mike Karanikolas, Revolve (NASDAQ:RVLV) is a fashion retailer leveraging social media and a community of fashion influencers to drive its merchandising strategy.

Why Do We Think RVLV Will Underperform?

May need to improve its platform and marketing strategy as its 5.4% average growth in active customers underwhelmed Expensive marketing campaigns hurt its profitability and make us wonder what would happen if it let up on the gas Flat earnings per share over the last three years lagged its peers

At $27.22 per share, Revolve trades at 17.3x forward EV/EBITDA. Read our free research report to see why you should think twice about including RVLV in your portfolio, it’s free.

Teladoc (TDOC)

Market Cap: $1.07 billion

Founded to help people in rural areas get online medical consultations, Teladoc Health (NYSE:TDOC) is a telemedicine platform that facilitates remote doctor’s visits.

Why Do We Think Twice About TDOC?

Annual revenue growth of 1.7% over the last three years was below our standards for the consumer internet sector Customer spending has dipped by 8.5% on average as it focused on growing its users Projected sales are flat for the next 12 months, implying demand will slow from its three-year trend

Teladoc’s stock price of $5.90 implies a valuation ratio of 4.5x forward EV/EBITDA. To fully understand why you should be careful with TDOC, check out our full research report (it’s free).

One Consumer Internet Stock to Watch:

Take-Two (TTWO)

Market Cap: $40.4 billion

Best known for its Grand Theft Auto and NBA 2K franchises, Take Two (NASDAQ:TTWO) is one of the world’s largest video game publishers.

Why Is TTWO Interesting?

Market share is on track to rise over the next 12 months as its 28% projected revenue growth implies demand will accelerate from its three-year trend Excellent EBITDA margin of 14.9% highlights the efficiency of its business model Free cash flow margin jumped by 4.9 percentage points over the last few years, giving the company more resources to pursue growth initiatives, repurchase shares, or pay dividends

title: Stock Market Today, April 21: Hims & Hers Health Drops as Amazon Unveils Competing Weight Loss Program
content:
Hims & Hers Health(NYSE:HIMS), the consumer-focused telehealth platform, closed Tuesday at $29.76, down 4.03%. The stock declined during the regular session after Amazon(NASDAQ:AMZN) launched a competing GLP-1 weight-loss program, though it has still gained 39.33% in the past week.

Trading volume reached 56.7 million shares, about 50% above its three-month average of 37.8 million shares. Hims & Hers Health IPO'd in 2019 and has grown 204% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500(SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 0.63% to 7,064, while the Nasdaq Composite(NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) slipped 0.59% to 24,260. Within telehealth and online health services, peers Teladoc Health (NYSE:TDOC) fell 1.64% to close at $6.00, and American Well(NYSE:AMWL) finished down 4.54% at $6.31, underscoring sentiment pressures across virtual care names.

What this means for investors

Hims & Hers stock pulled back after posting significant gains in the past five days. The stock had rallied on news that the FDA might shift its peptide policy, and an agreement with Novo Nordisk(NYSE:NVO) that ended a legal dispute between the two over weight-loss drugs.

However, today’s news that Amazon One Medical would move into that same anti-obesity drug space undermined some of the benefits of its agreement with Novo, and caused the rally to falter. Amazon’s same-day delivery could compete with Hims & Hers’ services, and undermine a core part of its business.

Investors will be watching Amazon’s new offer and its potential impact on Hims revenue and subscriber numbers when Hims & Hers announces its Q1 results on May 11.
